notes: Source networks of the EVM bridges (rounds 16 and 17). `launch` is the launch status of each network; it is recorded a second time in tools/evm-nets/launch.py and every tool refuses a network whose `launch.v1` is false, or every network when the two records disagree (review R329-EVM-1). `feeRecipient` and `feeBps` are the owner's fee address and rates (5 + 5 bps), which the deploy tools require of every vault config of these networks (R329-EVM-2). `signer` is what all signers of one network share: eth_half.py and vigia.py take it by chain id and refuse an operator file that contradicts it (R329-EVM-3); `interval_s`, `max_release_signs_per_hour` and `refused_retry` are the daemon pacing for that network's window (R329-EVM-6). `timing` is what a release round is held to (R329-EVM-4): the join window is anchor_max_age x anchorBlockSeconds; a signature whose work or anchor age reaches alertFraction of it is alerted, and a signer whose recent work per signature exceeds holdFraction of it starts no round. Asset addresses were read on-chain and against the issuer's own page on 2026-11-16 (agents/320-bridge-evm-nets-r16.md section 2). `rpc` is a public read-only endpoint used only as the fork source of local rehearsals; operators use their own nodes. Block times and finality lags are measurements of 2026-11-16, not guarantees. Every network takes ProvenanceSourceVault byte-identical to the Ethereum bridge.

launch.reason: Fit for v1 (reviews 325 and 329): the join window is 200 Ethereum block numbers (2,400 s); five serial cold signatures use about 5% of it.

signer.why: depth 2 Ethereum block numbers (24 s of a 51 min window): ArbOS fills the value for a number only once it has seen the next one
signer.pacing_why: window 200 x 12 s = 2,400 s (Ethereum block numbers): the Ethereum bridge pacing and budgets fit unchanged

finality.meaning: its batch is in a finalized Ethereum block

launch.reason: Held until one release lands inside the 256-block window (about 51 s; 49 s to join) with the production signer path at 0.2 s blocks. Measured by reviewer 329 on a paced fork, signers one after another: paid at 31.6 s of 49 s only with 4 s of work per signature (every signer warm); not paid in 300 s with 12 s of work (5 rounds, at most 4 signatures); not paid in 301 s with 26 s of work, the cold-cache rebuild of today (4 rounds, at most 2 signatures).

signer.why: depth 5 blocks (1 s of 51 s): 0.2 s blocks, so five blocks cost 2% of the window and cover a one-second reordering of the newest blocks
signer.pacing_why: window 250 x 0.2 s = 50 s: 5 s passes; a round lives 50 s, so the hourly budget is 18 rounds and a refused round is tried again after 12 s (not launchable: values for rehearsals only)

finality.meaning: its batch is in a finalized Ethereum block

signer.pacing_why: window 250 x 2 s = 500 s: 20 s passes (two passes are 8% of the window); a refused round is tried again after a quarter of the window; six rounds an hour cover 50 minutes of consecutive misses
